status: declared by the pull request that closes #1321 before any score was computed; a development study, never a verdict. (s3c-ann-net) stays the candidate of avenue #1318 and (s3c) stays the H5 candidate: nothing here changes either. Nothing is registered or published: no record in docs/runs/ is edited, the live record and its pin do not change, no declaration already merged changes (metadata/s3c_announced_settlement_1288.json, metadata/s3c_ann_net_diagnosis_1319.json, metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json, metadata/net_settlement.json, metadata/sources.json and docs/decisions/information-set.md included), docs/research/h5-candidate.json and scripts/final_test_preregistration.py do not change, no day after 2026-09-03 is scored and no lockbox day is scored. Amendments made after a number was computed are listed in `amendments`; there are none.
ruling: Eleonora, 30 October 2026, chat, relayed on #1321: on #1318, test both the flag-plus-net arm and a gross-sized arm. The net x scarcity interaction in #1318 is not part of this ruling and is left out.
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, two arms on the candidate (s3c-ann-net). Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)
why: #1320 found that the flag (s3c-ann) and the net (s3c-ann-net) win in different places. Netting shrinks the fitted settlement shift: in 2018-19 the realised settlement-day premium was +6.0 bp [+3.3, +9.3], the flag learned +2.02 bp and the net +0.48 bp. On coupon days, maturing amounts do not offset gross one for one (g + m +1.59 bp per USD 100 bn [+0.81, +2.67] at lead 1, H-a supported for the coupon leg); for the bill leg H-a is undecided. The two arms test the two readings: keep the flag and add the net beside it, or size the coupon leg by the gross it finances.
decision_instant: 18:00 America/New_York on the decision day (repo_model.decision_instant.DECISION_TIME, amended on 29 October 2026, #1312). Every walk of this study, the references included, is made at that instant; no figure of #1288's record (made at 16:00) is reproduced or edited. An announcement stamped 12:00 on its announcemt_date is public from 12:00, so any decision instant from 12:00 to 23:59 counts the same auctions and the announced sums do not depend on the move from 16:00

candidates.name: sc_s3c_ann_flagnet
candidates.label: (s3c-ann-flagnet)
candidates.definition: (s3c-ann) with #1273's announced net beside each flag. Per leg, two terms: the announced 0/1 flag of (s3c-ann) (1 when the offering amounts of the leg's auctions settling on the target day T that had been announced by the decision instant of D = T - h sum to more than zero) and the signed announced net of the leg on T (net coupon, net bill), in units of USD 100 bn, read at the same instant. Four settlement terms in all. The terms enter the fit at every lead h = 1..5 when at least three training pairs carry them (the flags as every flag of the fit, the nets when non-zero); the flags come first in the design and the nets after them. Everything else is (s3)'s: the other terms, the Huber fit (k = 1.345), the ridge of 5, the pool of standardised residuals and the direct pairs; the SRF cap at the line from full allotment, margin 0 bp, is applied to its quantiles exactly as to (s3)'s (repo_model.s3c_candidate, unchanged). At lead 1 the flag is the panel's flag as (s3c) reads it and the net is #1273's.
candidates.module: repo_model.s3c_announced (FLAGNET_ARM = sc.ARMS[2] renamed with extra = (net_coupon, net_bill); AnnouncedTermTable for the flags, AnnouncedSizeTerms for the nets); the fit is repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar's with its `extra` terms generalised to the size names (SIZE_EXTRAS, EXTRA_TERMS); no behaviour of an existing arm changes
candidates.units: flag: 0/1; net_coupon, net_bill: USD 100 bn (a net coupon settlement of USD 30 bn reads 0.30; the sign is kept, more maturing than settling reads negative); effect reported in bp per flagged day and bp per USD 100 bn

candidates.name: sc_s3c_ann_gross
candidates.label: (s3c-ann-gross)
candidates.definition: (s3c-ann) with the coupon leg sized by the announced gross offering amount in place of its flag: the coupon term is the sum of the offering amounts of the coupon auctions settling on T that had been announced by the decision instant of D = T - h, in units of USD 100 bn (zero where none is announced), read at every lead h = 1..5. The bill leg is the announced 0/1 flag of (s3c-ann), as there. This arm has no net term and no coupon flag. Everything else is (s3)'s, the cap is (s3c)'s, and the fit is the same as above.
candidates.module: repo_model.s3c_announced (GROSS_ARM = sc.ARMS[2] renamed with the coupon flag dropped from its terms and extra = (gross_coupon,); AnnouncedTermTable for the bill flag, AnnouncedSizeTerms for the gross coupon)
candidates.units: gross_coupon: USD 100 bn (a USD 40 bn coupon offering reads 0.40); effect reported in bp per USD 100 bn of gross coupon offering. The size is plain (no scarcity state multiplies it), as in (s3c-ann-net)

new_read.what: the announced gross coupon offering as a size (`gross_coupon`), and the announced net as an extra term beside a flag (`net_coupon`, `net_bill`)
new_read.availability: an auction's offering amount and settlement date are public from 12:00 America/New_York on its announcemt_date (metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json, #541, measured and off; the same records as repo_model.net_settlement reads). The figure for target day T at lead h counts an auction only when its announcement is at or before the decision instant of the panel day h rows before T. A training pair reads the figure of its own decision (T - h), so a training figure and a forecast figure are the same function of the same announcements
new_read.leakage_boundary: repo_model.s3c_announced.AnnouncedSizeTerms.read re-derives the gross figure from the announced auctions at the decision instant and compares it with the figure the table serves: a figure that counts an auction announced after that instant raises LookAheadError, one that leaves an announced auction out raises StaleReadError; the net is re-checked by AnnouncedNetSizeTable.read (#1288). tests/test_s3c_announced_sizes_1321.py holds the leakage test with one recorded mutation (the instant of the figure taken from the target day instead of the decision day; LookAheadError). The coupon-leg and net reads of #1288 are covered by tests/test_s3c_announced.py
new_read.caveat: Lens E's caveat (docs/reviews/2026-10-19-five-lens/lens-E-data-plumbing.md, item G) applies to the bill leg of both arms and to the net bill of (s3c-ann-flagnet): Treasury publishes no clock time for an announcement and the 12:00 instant of a cash management bill is unverified. It is said on the page and not removed
new_read.not_read_elsewhere: no published declaration, record or live path reads it; (s3c)'s own table still serves a settlement at lead 1 only (tests/test_s3c_announced.py)

The 2026 days are reported on their own, as a window

The study checks that (s3c-ann) equals (s3c) cell for cell at lead 1 and that every scored decision day has a forecast of every model, and refuses to write a record otherwise

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
primary.calibration: the coverage of the central 90% band (q5 to q95, closed) of every model, pooled and by regime; a rate, reported as a mean and not tested
primary.comparisons: each new arm against (s3c-ann-net) (the candidate), against (s3c) and against (s3c-ann), paired; the benchmarks B1, B1' and B2 are not part of this directive's comparisons and are not re-scored here

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1321, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): an arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.splits: pooled; by lead; by regime (the declared regimes, 2018-19 and 2020 on their own among them); by pressure-day type of the target day (turn_days.reporting_day_type, the record in force); by the settlement-day type of the target at each lead h = 1..5 (a coupon settlement day, a bill settlement day, a day with neither: the panel's gross settlement above zero on the target day). The 2026 development days are the second window and carry the same splits. The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested against it; a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

shift_against_premium.what: for each arm of #1288 and of this study, the fitted settlement shift on settlement-day targets against the realised settlement-day premium, by regime of the target day, as #1320 did (table 4b of scripts/s3c_ann_net_diagnosis_1319.py)
shift_against_premium.definitions: over the cells (decision day, lead) of the scored decision days: the fitted shift is the standardised shift of the refit the forecast used (all settlement terms, flags and sizes) times the scale at the anchor in bp, averaged over the cells whose target day is a settlement day (the panel's gross coupon or bill settlement above zero); the realised premium is the mean realised spread on settlement-day targets less that on the other targets; the bias is the mean error (realised less the forecast median) on settlement-day targets less that on the others
shift_against_premium.leads: h = 2 to 5 (where #1288's arms differ from (s3c)) as #1320 did, and h = 1 on its own (where the new arms differ from (s3c-ann-net))
shift_against_premium.interval: the 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over decision days (block 10, 2000 replications, seed 1321) of each statistic; an interval over days that share refits, not a sampling interval for a coefficient; a regime with fewer than 20 decision days is shown without one
shift_against_premium.fitted_effect: the fitted effect of each settlement term in bp (per flagged day, or per USD 100 bn), by lead and regime of the target day: the mean over the scored decision days of the refit the forecast used times the anchor's scale, with the share of days on which the term was in the fit

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c-ann-net) stays the candidate of avenue #1318 and (s3c) the H5 candidate until she rules.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and settlement-day-type splits beside it.
If an arm should replace (s3c-ann-net), that goes to her as a marked question with numbered options and a default that changes no claim; the candidate does not change in this directive.
The bill leg is read with Lens E's caveat on the announcement time of a cash management bill.
